definition: Input the tokenizer cannot represent as known units.
details: Input the tokenizer cannot represent as known units. Byte-level fallback has largely eliminated hard OOV failures, but rare strings still fragment into many tokens, degrading modeling quality.

explainer.lead: Out-of-vocabulary describes input the tokenizer cannot represent as known units. Rare strings now usually fragment into many tokens rather than failing outright, which still hurts modeling quality.

tiers.eli5: It's like a dictionary that has no entry for a new slang word, so it spells it out letter by letter.
tiers.practitioner: Byte-level fallback means unknown words rarely crash tokenization, but they splinter into many tokens and inflate sequence length and cost. Watch for rare names, codes, and non-Latin scripts degrading quality.
tiers.paperLevel: A token is OOV when it is absent from the tokenizer vocabulary. Byte-level fallback largely eliminates hard OOV failures, but rare strings still fragment into many tokens, degrading modeling quality.

explainer.example: A username like 'xq7_zz9' not in the vocabulary is split into several subword or byte tokens, consuming more context than a common word would.
